stories.title: Fortune Secures Equity Partner for Casa Tua Miami Condo
stories.excerpt: Three years after launching sales for the Casa Tua-branded condo development in Miami’s Brickell district, Fortune International Group has found an equity partner in One United Properties. The Romanian development firm has invested $43 million into the 77-story ORA by Casa Tua development. The 533-unit tower will rise at 1210 Brickell Avenue, near the corner with Southeast 13th Street, across the street from Fortune International Group’s headquarters. Construction is expected to begin in the first quarter of 2027. Since 2025, Fortune International Group, led by Edgardo Defortuna, has been accepting investment through the EB-5 program, which provides U.S. residency to foreign investors. The firm purchased the 1-acre site for $30 million in 2024, a year after launching condo sales. A representative for the developer did not immediately disclose current sales figures. Units will be delivered fully furnished. The project marks the first branded residential tower for Casa Tua, an Italian hospitality concept founded by married couple Micky and Leticia Grendene. “After many months analyzing deals of all shapes and sizes, ORA stood out for its prime Brickell location, approved development plans, strong pre-sales and world-class partners,” David Flusberg, One United Properties’ U.S. managing partner, said in a statement. Founded in 2007, One United Properties went public on the Bucharest Stock Exchange in 2021. Today, the company has a market capitalization of about $780 million. The equity investment comes less than a month after Fortune International Group obtained a slew of construction debt for luxury condo projects in Miami-Dade County. Just last week, the Miami-based firm secured Florida’s biggest construction loan: $817 million for the Faena-branded, waterfront development in Downtown Miami. It also nabbed $463 million to finish the oceanfront St. Regis Residences in Sunny Isles Beach and a $220 million predevelopment loan for a waterfront project on Key Biscayn
bullets: One United Properties (Romania) invests $43M equity into Fortune's 533-unit ORA by Casa Tua condo, Miami Brickell
77-story tower at 1210 Brickell Ave breaks ground Q1 2027; using EB-5 foreign investor residency program

stories.summary: One United Properties has committed $43 million in equity to Fortune International Group's ORA by Casa Tua, a 533-unit luxury condo tower in Miami's Brickell district launching construction in Q1 2027. Fortune acquired the 1-acre site for $30 million in 2024 and has been accepting EB-5 foreign investor capital since 2025. Units will deliver fully furnished as the brand's first residential tower.
stories.impact: Foreign capital inflow signals persistent Miami condo demand despite recent market softness; EB-5 financing availability reduces developer reliance on traditional debt and equity markets. Brickell's density and proximity to Fortune's HQ make it a lower-risk infill play, but the EB-5 structure suggests traditional financing may remain constrained or uncompetitive in the condo-for-sale segment.

stories.title: Greybrook Picks Up 334-Unit Mansfield Rental Community
stories.excerpt: The Greybrook U.S. Multifamily Income & Growth Fund acquired Evolv, a 334-unit multifamily property in Mansfield. Greybrook landed a $39.2 million acquisition loan from Greystone as part of the deal. The fixed-rate Fannie Mae loan carries a five-year term, with three years of interest-only payments followed by a 35-year amortization schedule. Greystone’s financing team included Richard Kourbage, Garvin Lee, and Gillian McIlroy. Cushman & Wakefield’s Investment Sales team, Grant Raymond and Asher Hall, represented the seller, Advenir Living, in the transaction. Cushman & Wakefield’s debt professionals included Chase Johnson and Caleb Riebe.Built in 2012, Evolv is a garden-style multifamily community situated on approximately 18.6 acres at 370 North State Highway 360 in Mansfield. The property features private patios or balconies. Community amenities include a resort-style swimming pool, 24-hour fitness center, clubhouse, outdoor kitchen, playground, dog park and garage parking.Mansfield is located southwest of Dallas and southeast of Fort Worth. bullets: Greybrook U.S. Multifamily Income & Growth Fund acquires 334-unit Evolv in Mansfield, Texas for undisclosed price

stories.summary: Greybrook's multifamily fund acquired Evolv, a 334-unit garden-style apartment community in Mansfield, Texas, built in 2012. Greystone provided a $39.2 million Fannie Mae fixed-rate loan with a 5-year term, including 3 years of interest-only payments and a 35-year amortization. Cushman & Wakefield brokered the transaction for seller Advenir Living.
stories.impact: Fannie Mae's continued lending at competitive terms on stabilized Texas rentals signals healthy secondary-market multifamily debt availability and appetite. Mansfield's suburban DFW location and Greybrook's fund structure indicate confidence in steady rent growth and long-hold value-add potential in mid-market Texas suburbs.

stories.title: Helaba Lends $82M on Macy’s-to-Residential Conversion Project Near Denver
stories.excerpt: Alliance Residential Company has secured $82.2 million of construction financing for its multifamily makeover of a vacant Macy’s department store in a Denver suburb, Commercial Observer has learned. German commercial bank Helaba supplied the loan for Alliance’s 358-unit apartment complex at a former Macy’s store within the Streets at SouthGlenn shopping center in Centennial, Colo. Alliance acquired the shuttered department store for $11 million. Jason Deck, director of real estate finance at Helaba, noted that Alliance has experience transforming Macy’s sites into multifamily and is redeveloping a similar conversion project in Hillsboro, Ore. Deck said the deal served as a win-win for both Alliance and the seller, PCCP, which owns the retail property as part of a joint venture. “It’s great for the seller as they’re going to bring 350-plus market-rate units to the center, and it’s great for Alliance because you have this built-in amenity set already there,” Deck told CO. He added that a Whole Foods grocery store was “a stone’s throw away” from the development. Deck added that the Centennial submarket has strong multifamily fundamentals with its location 12 miles south of Downtown Denver. The project, which is slated for completion in September 2029, will have resident amenities that include a swimming pool, coworking spaces, a fitness center and a rooftop deck. Alliance Residential did not immediately return a request for comment. Andrew Coen can be reached at acoen@commercialobserver.com
bullets: Alliance Residential secures $82.2M construction financing from Helaba (German bank) for 358-unit Macy's conversion in Centennial, Colorado
Converted shuttered Macy's at Streets at SouthGlenn shopping center; Alliance acquired building for $11M
Alliance replicating Macy's-to-multifamily playbook in Hillsboro, Oregon; lender notes built-in retail/amenity synergies
stories.summary: German commercial bank Helaba provided $82.2 million in construction financing to Alliance Residential for a 358-unit multifamily conversion of a vacant Macy's department store at the Streets at SouthGlenn shopping center in Centennial, Colorado. Alliance acquired the defunct anchor tenant for $11 million and is applying the same conversion strategy to a similar property in Hillsboro, Oregon. The deal capitalized on existing retail infrastructure and parking.
stories.impact: Macy's closures and anchor-tenant vacancies in established suburban retail centers create low-cost land and structural acquisition opportunities for experienced adaptive-reuse developers. Denver metro's continued rental demand and Helaba's willingness to finance non-traditional underwriting suggest capital recognizes conversion risk is lower than ground-up building and entitlement costs. Proliferation of this playbook could accelerate supply in tertiary submarkets.

stories.title: KMG Seeks Tysons Site for Proposed $250M MXU Development
stories.excerpt: Keyserling Management Group, LLC (KMG), led by Managing Member Joseph Michael, has retained SVN | Providence Realty Advisors to identify and evaluate existing buildings and development sites in Tysons, Virginia, for a proposed mixed-use development combining hospitality, residential, commercial, cultural, and educational facilities. The preliminary concept encompasses approximately 450,000 square feet, including 165 hotel suites, up to 200 apartment residences, offices, retail, dining, a public atrium, chapel theatre, landscaped park, and cultural institute. The estimated development costs range from $200 million to $250 million. “We envision the cultural institute as an active part of everyday life, with the atrium functioning as a public square for leisure, work, and cultural exchange,” said Michael. “Exhibitions and performances would bring together residents, hotel guests, researchers, and visitors.” KMG selected Tysons as its initial search area because of its proximity to Washington, D.C., four Metro Silver Line stations, and concentration of corporate headquarters, technology companies, and professional services. The post KMG Seeks Tysons Site for Proposed $250M MXU Development appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: KMG (led by Joseph Michael) seeks Tysons, Virginia site for $200–$250M mixed-use development via SVN Providence

stories.summary: Keyserling Management Group, led by Joseph Michael, has engaged SVN Providence Advisors to identify and evaluate development sites in Tysons, Virginia for a $200–$250 million mixed-use project combining 165 hotel suites, up to 200 apartment units, office, retail, dining, cultural programming, and public spaces. KMG selected Tysons for its proximity to Washington, D.C., Silver Line Metro access, and clustering of corporate and technology tenants.
stories.impact: Mixed-use development pursuit in Tysons signals developer confidence in suburban DC's continued job growth and demographic appeal; 200-unit residential component suggests stable rental demand near Metro and corporate campuses. Blended hospitality-residential program indicates developer is hedging apartment-only risk while capturing white-collar population migration to Tysons' tech and professional services hubs. Site scarcity in Tysons may drive competitive pricing and longer entitlement timelines.

stories.title: Townhouse Brokerage Leslie Garfield Inks Office Lease in Brooklyn Heights
stories.excerpt: Leslie Garfield, a New York City-focused townhouse brokerage, has relocated to a larger office along Montague Street in Brooklyn Heights, Commercial Observer has learned. Founded 50 years ago by Leslie J. Garfield, who died in 2022, the firm inked a “long-term,” 1,600-square-foot office lease covering the entire second floor of Owen Realty’s 156 Montague Street, a townhouse-style office property, a source close to the deal told CO. Leslie Garfield relocated from a smaller office space at 122 Montague Street. The firm also has an office at 505 Park Avenue in Midtown Manhattan. “Our former space at 122 Montague Street served us well, but as our Brooklyn business continued to grow, we needed a larger space to accommodate our expanding team,” Matthew Lesser, senior partner at Leslie Garfield, told CO. “We are particularly pleased to have secured a long-term lease along Montague Street, one of Brooklyn Heights’ most established retail corridors, which has seen renewed activity and increased demand. The new space reflects our continued investment in Brooklyn and reinforces our commitment to serving the borough’s townhouse market for years to come.” The asking rent was $77 per square foot. JLL negotiated the deal for the landlord, but the names of the brokers who worked on the lease were not immediately available. Jeffrey Lopez from Lee & Associates brokered the deal on behalf of the tenant. Some of the firm’s recent townhouse sales include the $9.4 million sale of 374 Washington Avenue, a 7,000-square-foot, five-bedroom townhouse in historic Clinton Hill, Brooklyn. The firm also lists the former home of art historian Susan Weber Soros at 116 East 70th Street on Manhattan’s Upper East Side as one of the properties it is selling for $22.5 million. At 156 Montague Street, Leslie Garfield will join baby stroller brand Uppababy, which signed a lease for 3,780 square feet of retail space at the base of the property in September. Amanda Schiavo can be reached at aschia
bullets: Leslie Garfield (50-year-old NYC townhouse brokerage) relocates to 1,600 SF second floor at 156 Montague Street, Brooklyn Heights

stories.summary: Leslie Garfield, a New York City–focused townhouse brokerage founded 50 years ago, has signed a long-term lease for 1,600 square feet on the second floor of 156 Montague Street in Brooklyn Heights. The relocation from nearby 122 Montague Street reflects the firm's expanding Brooklyn business and renewed activity along Montague Street, one of Brooklyn Heights' established retail corridors.
stories.impact: Minimal multifamily development relevance; story reflects office leasing dynamics and retail corridor vitality in Brooklyn Heights but does not signal residential demand, supply, capital, or cost factors material to multifamily underwriting.

stories.title: Legacy, CrossHarbor Teaming Up on 444-Unit Richardson Apartment Community
stories.excerpt: Legacy Partners, together with their equity partner CrossHarbor Capital Partners, has acquired a 10.4-acre site in Richardson, Texas, with plans to develop Legacy Arapaho, a 444-residence apartment community. The partnership recently closed on the site at 250 E. Arapaho Rd. with a construction loan from First United Bank of Durant, Oklahoma. The existing vacant two-story office building will be demolished. Rampart Multifamily, Inc., based in Grapevine, is the general contractor. Legacy Arapaho recently broke ground and anticipates the start of leasing and initial occupancy spring 2028, and final completion by spring 2029. Legacy Arapaho is Legacy’s third apartment community development in Richardson, following Ovation at Galatyn Park which opened in 2024 and Galatyn Station (fka The Venue) which opened in 2008. Since 2023, Legacy delivered 880 LYN on Lake Carolyn in Las Colinas’ Urban Center, Merit in Lewisville, Ovation at Galatyn Park in Richardson, and Rylan at Gateway in Forney, as well as two single-family build-to-rent communities which made their debut last year. The post Legacy, CrossHarbor Teaming Up on 444-Unit Richardson Apartment Community appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Legacy Partners and CrossHarbor Capital Partners acquire 10.4-acre Richardson, Texas site for 444-unit apartment community
Legacy Arapaho breaks ground; First United Bank (Durant, OK) provides construction loan; leasing starts Spring 2028

stories.summary: Legacy Partners and equity partner CrossHarbor Capital Partners have closed on a 10.4-acre site in Richardson, Texas at 250 E. Arapaho Road to develop Legacy Arapaho, a 444-unit apartment community. The partnership secured a construction loan from First United Bank of Durant, Oklahoma, demolished the existing two-story office building, and broke ground with Rampart Multifamily as general contractor. Leasing and initial occupancy are expected in Spring 2028, with final completion by Spring 2029.
stories.impact: Legacy's third Richardson development in 16 years (plus 4 other DFW communities since 2023) signals strong rental fundamentals and repeat developer appetite in north Dallas suburbs. Replacement of vacant office with residential converts underutilized Class B commercial space and capitalizes on suburban job corridor concentration. Consistent delivery pace suggests Richardson submarket rental growth is absorbing new supply—favorable for new entrants but signals tightening windows for land acquisition.

stories.title: Tishman’s 110 East 16th Street Development Site Sells for $44M

Developer and general contractor Pro-H Group paid Tishman $44.25 million for the site, a source familiar with the transaction told Commercial Observer. Pro-H, led by founder Burton Hung, plans to replace the site’s existing parking garage with a 52-unit residential condominium building. The acquisition and development plans were announced Monday by Pro-H and Northwind Group. A blueprint sketch of 110 East 16th Street. RENDERING: Morris Adjmi Architects via DOB Now The Union Square site last traded to Tishman in 2015. bullets: Pro-H Group (Burton Hung) purchases Tishman's 110 East 16th Street development site near Union Square for $44.25M

stories.summary: Pro-H Group, led by founder Burton Hung, acquired Tishman Realty's long-held 110 East 16th Street development site near Union Square for $44.25 million to develop a 52-unit residential condo building replacing a parking garage. Northwind Group supplied a $30 million first-mortgage acquisition and predevelopment loan. Pro-H and Northwind highlighted Manhattan's record-low new condo inventory and limited supply pipeline as the core investment thesis.
stories.impact: Manhattan's decade-low condo inventory and tight supply signal sustained pricing power and development velocity despite higher interest rates; the $9.25M appreciation over 11 years (2015–2025) and ease of debt financing imply investor confidence in Union Square submarket liquidity and end-user demand. Limited new supply favors earlier-stage projects, but high acquisition prices ($850k/unit basis pre-construction) compress feasibility unless rents or condo price growth materialize faster than underwriting assumptions.

stories.title: Southern Management Launches Modernization of Charles Plaza in Downtown Baltimore
stories.excerpt: Southern Management Companies has launched a multi-year modernization of Charles Plaza, one of the largest residential and mixed-use complexes in downtown Baltimore. Working with Baltimore-based WorkShop Development, the company plans to upgrade the property’s retail, office space and public areas, as well as the three apartment buildings, in phases over the coming years. As part of the effort, Southern Management has retained MacKenzie Commercial to lead retail leasing and repositioning. The first phase, a $1 million upgrade to the complex’s facade, signage and outdoor amenities, is scheduled for completion in early 2027. Charles Plaza occupies a prominent position in the heart of downtown, with 857 apartments as well as retail, office and parking facilities. The project is being undertaken with support from the Downtown Partnership of Baltimore, and the team includes BCT Architects, which is leading the design. and JC Porter Construction, which is serving as general contractor. The post Southern Management Launches Modernization of Charles Plaza in Downtown Baltimore appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Southern Management Companies launches multi-year modernization of Charles Plaza in downtown Baltimore; 857 apartments + retail, office, parking
Phase 1: $1M facade, signage, outdoor amenity upgrade completing early 2027; phased rollout with WorkShop Development
MacKenzie Commercial leading retail repositioning; BCT Architects designing; JC Porter Construction as GC; Downtown Partnership support
stories.summary: Southern Management Companies has begun a multi-year modernization campaign at Charles Plaza, one of downtown Baltimore's largest residential and mixed-use complexes, encompassing 857 apartments, retail, office, and parking. Phase 1, a $1 million upgrade to facade, signage, and outdoor amenities, is scheduled for completion in early 2027. The effort is undertaken with Baltimore-based WorkShop Development, retail consultant MacKenzie Commercial, designer BCT Architects, and general contractor JC Porter Construction.
stories.impact: Value-add repositioning of large downtown Baltimore asset signals landlord confidence in urban core demand recovery and retail/office market stabilization. Phased approach limits disruption to occupied units and spreads capital deployment, reducing risk of underperformance. Downtown Partnership support suggests policy/tax incentive backing, which could enable higher reinvestment rates. Success will be a key test of Baltimore's post-COVID multifamily absorption and retail leasing health.

stories.title: Streaming Platform Vimeo Signs 15K-SF Lease at Haymes’ 5 Penn Plaza
stories.excerpt: A video streaming platform is moving its New York City headquarters within the Penn District. Vimeo, owned by Italian tech firm Bending Spoons, signed a 15,172-square-foot lease on part of the 15th floor of Haymes Investment Company’s 5 Penn Plaza, according to the brokers on both sides of the deal. Vimeo will be relocating from the 10th floor of 330 West 34th Street, about half a block away from its new Penn Plaza office. Asking rent and the length of the lease were not immediately disclosed, but the average office asking rent for Midtown in the third quarter of 2026 was $85.53 per square foot, according to a CBRE report. “The neighborhood has emerged as one of Manhattan’s premier office destinations, driven by significant investment in modernized buildings, transit improvements and an expanding mix of amenities,” Avison Young’s Alexis Odgers, who represented the tenant alongside Joe Gervino and Larry Zuckerman, said in a statement. “At 5 Penn Plaza, Vimeo secured a highly efficient, amenity-rich headquarters that supports its long-term workplace needs while reaffirming the district’s appeal to innovative technology and media companies.” JLL’s Mitchell Konsker, Daniel Turkewitz, Greg Wang, Christine Colley, Kristen Morgan and Kate Roush negotiated on behalf of Haymes Investment Company. “Vimeo is an exciting addition to 5 Penn and a meaningful transaction for the building,” Konsker said in a statement. “This deal confirms that well-positioned, amenity-rich buildings are winning in this market.” Other tenants in the building include CFC USA, the U.S. arm of a London-based cybersecurity protection insurance provider, which signed a 13,065-square-foot lease in April, and cryptocurrency security platform Fireblocks, which signed a 35,000-square-foot lease in July 2025. Mark Hallum can be reached at mhallum@commercialobserver.com.

stories.summary: Video streaming platform Vimeo, owned by Italian tech firm Bending Spoons, signed a 15,172-square-foot lease on the 15th floor of 5 Penn Plaza in Manhattan, relocating from nearby 330 West 34th Street. The long-term deal reflects average Midtown office asking rents of approximately $85.53 per square foot (Q3 2026). Brokers highlighted the Penn District's modernized buildings, transit access, and expanding amenities as key attractions.
stories.impact: Minimal multifamily relevance; story signals office market stability and intra-district tenant movement in Midtown Manhattan, not residential demand or supply dynamics. Penn District office renovation and tenant retention are positive for surrounding mixed-use and hospitality, but do not directly inform multifamily underwriting.

stories.title: Madis Coffee Opens New Philadelphia Location
stories.excerpt: Madis Coffee, a specialty coffee roastery and café chain, has officially opened its newest Philadelphia location. Located at 210 South 12th Street, this marks the chain’s third new cafe in Center City in two years. The new location occupies approximately 1,984 square feet on the ground floor of 210 South 12th, a luxury residential building right in the heart of Midtown. Owned by New York-based developer Midwood Investment & Development, the building will soon be home to Sushi by Scratch Restaurants and NADC Burger. Also currently in the building’s retail space is Salon Republic, a national salon studio concept. Located in the Midtown Village neighborhood of Center City, 210 South 12th features studio, one-, two-, and three-bedroom penthouse apartments. Madis Coffee Roasters operates four other locations across Philadelphia. The chain expansion began in late 2022, with stores offering fresh pastries and locally roasted coffee. stories.summary: Madis Coffee Roasters, a specialty coffee roastery and café chain, opened its third Center City Philadelphia location in two years at 210 South 12th Street, occupying 1,984 square feet on the ground floor of a Midwood Investment & Development luxury residential building. The building features studio through three-bedroom penthouses and houses additional retail tenants including Sushi by Scratch, NADC Burger, and Salon Republic. Madis operates five Philadelphia locations overall.

Story reflects end-user confidence in Philadelphia Center City residential absorption rather than development fundamentals.
